recommendations.title: The "Advisory residue never flips an exit code" bullet under `## What is deliberately not enforced` in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.m
recommendations.body: The "Advisory residue never flips an exit code" bullet under `## What is deliberately not enforced` in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md` (step 3 "Write ROADMAP_FORMAT.md specifying both artifacts and naming the code that enforces them") says exit **1** happens "when a stage exhausts its retry budget without clearing its gates", but `roadmap.py:_run_stage` spends an attempt on three failure kinds — `FAILURE_INVOKE` (backend rc≠0 or an empty reply), `FAILURE_PARSE` (a reply carrying no liftable or parseable artifact), and `FAILURE_GATES` — and any of them reaches `OUTCOME_STAGE_EXHAUSTED` and rc 1. `RoadmapResult.failure_kind` exists precisely to stop that misreading (its comment: a backend failing rc≠0 every attempt otherwise "reads as 'the model disagreed with the gates'"), so the doc teaches the confusion the code guards against; the same sentence also scopes exit **2** to "before any stage is invoked", while `_render_stage_prompt` raises `RoadmapError` for a missing prompt template from inside `_run_stage`, after an earlier stage may already have written its artifact
recommendations.suggested_action: in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md`'s `## What is deliberately not enforced` exit-code bullet, restate exit 1 as a stage spending its budget without producing a usable artifact (no usable reply, an unparseable artifact, or unresolved violations) and drop the "before any stage is invoked" qualifier from exit 2

recommendations.title: `## Path convention` in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md` (step 3 "Write ROADMAP_FORMAT.md specifying both artifacts and naming the co
recommendations.body: `## Path convention` in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md` (step 3 "Write ROADMAP_FORMAT.md specifying both artifacts and naming the code that enforces them") names `plan_tool/locator.py:PLANS_SUBPATH` as "only the default the discovery walk finds" and stops there, but `cli/roadmap_cmd.py:cmd_roadmap` falls back to `create.py:resolve_output_dir` (`DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR`) when `resolve_explicit_plans_dir` returns `None`, so the one constant the section names is never consulted by this verb. A reader asking where roadmap artifacts land without `--plans-dir` gets a pointer to the wrong symbol; the two constants hold the same value, so nothing misbehaves today
recommendations.suggested_action: name `plan_tool/create.py:resolve_output_dir` as the `roadmap` verb's fallback in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md`'s `## Path convention`, alongside the existing `PLANS_SUBPATH` sentence
